commits.message:
feat(docs): VitePress Demos section with live xterm.js terminals (rich-demo-site-pek.4)

Surface every browser-bundled demo as a runnable page inside the existing
docs site. One pipeline (npm run docs:build), one deploy (docs.yml +
gh-pages-multiplexer), one source of truth for the demo list (the manifest
the bundle pipeline writes).

- vite.config.demos.ts: output to docs/public/demos-app/ so VitePress's
  public-files convention copies bundles to dist/demos-app/ verbatim; also
  emit docs/.vitepress/demos.json (the canonical demo list).
- docs/demos/[demo].md + [demo].paths.ts: VitePress dynamic-route page
  that iframes /demos-app/<name>/, with paths derived from the manifest.
- docs/demos/index.md: landing page listing all demos from the same
  manifest — adding/removing a demo updates the index automatically.
- docs/.vitepress/config.ts: read manifest at config-load, add Demos nav
  + sidebar section. No second list to maintain.
- package.json: docs:build / docs:dev chain demos:build first; demos.json
  is a precondition, not a fallback. Missing manifest fails loud.
- .gitignore: docs/public/demos-app/ + docs/.vitepress/demos.json are
  build artifacts; dist-demos/ is retired.

Verified via Chrome MCP against docs:preview: index lists 7 demos with
correct /rich-js/ base; rich-strip + themes-and-color-studio both load
status="ready", xterm-screen rendered with content, zero console errors.
8881/8881 vitest pass.

feat(demos): browser bundle pipeline + 7 demos refactored (rich-demo-site-pek.3) (#43)

* feat(demos): browser bundle pipeline + 7 demos refactored for host injection (rich-demo-site-pek.3)

Each demo splits into three files: app.ts (runDemo body taking a TerminalHost),
index.ts (node bootstrap), wire.ts (browser bootstrap). The node and browser
entrypoints differ only in which TerminalHost implementation they construct;
the demo logic is identical. [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow]

Bundle pipeline (vite.config.demos.ts): data-driven enumeration of
examples/*/wire.ts (paired with tsc-compiled dist-demo/examples/*/wire.js).
HTML + mount template in examples/_browser-shell/ stamped per demo into
.vite-demos/<name>/ at config time. [LAW:single-enforcer, one-source-of-truth]

Console-using demos route output through a new hostStream(host) adapter
(src/widgets/host-stream.ts) — a NodeJS.WritableStream-shaped wrapper whose
.write() forwards to host.write(). No Console-class change required.

Demos bundled for browser (7): browser-terminal-host-harness, rich-strip,
dropdown-demo, rich-config, rich-markup-plugins, themes-and-color-studio,
rich-template-bindings. Each verified in headless Chrome — first frame
renders, zero console errors.

Deferred (followups): claude-sessions (.3.1), rich-explore (.3.2), rich-dash
(.3.3) all reach node:fs/path/os/url directly; they need a FileSystem (and
SystemInfo) capability extracted before bundling. Console.saveText/saveHtml
and the prompt renderable's node:readline usage need the same lift-out (.3.4)
— stubbed for now via examples/_browser-shell/node-stub.js + a vite alias.

* fix(demos): bootstrap robustness — TDZ-safe onShutdown, try/finally, vite engines

Three concerns from PR #43 review:

1. **engines.node**: bump to `^20.19.0 || >=22.12.0` to match Vite 7.3.3's
   requirement (the `>=20` range allowed Node 20.0–20.18 which Vite rejects).

2. **TDZ-safe onShutdown for interactive bootstraps** (dropdown-demo,
   rich-config, rich-template-bindings): the `onShutdown` callback no longer
   references the `demo` binding. The demo body calls `handle.stop()` *before*
   invoking `onShutdown`, so the bootstrap callback only needs `host.stop()`
   + `process.exit(0)`. This removes the temporal-dead-zone window where a
   synchronous Ctrl-C inside `runDemo()` could reference an uninitialized
   `demo`. [LAW:types-are-the-program] the type of `onShutdown` shouldn't
   require a value that hasn't been bound yet.

3. **Cleanup on startup failure** (all 6 node bootstraps): wrap the
   `runDemo(host)` call in try/catch (interactive demos) or try/finally
   (one-shot demos) so `host.stop()` runs even if startup throws. Without
   this, a crash during construction would leave the terminal in alt-screen
   / raw mode.

Plus a focused unit test for `hostStream` pinning the
`.write(chunk) → host.write(chunk)` forwarding contract — the seam between
Console's existing `file:` option and any TerminalHost.

* fix(demos): try/catch around runDemo in browser wires + exitCode over exit(1)

Round-2 review findings, all the same architectural shape applied uniformly:

- Browser wires (6 files): `runDemo(host)` is now wrapped in `try/catch` that
  calls `host.stop()` and re-throws on startup failure. Mirrors the node
  bootstrap fix from the previous commit; same problem shape, same fix.
  [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] same code path either side; only the host
  implementation differs.

- themes-and-color-studio/index.ts: `process.exit(1)` inside the catch
  bypassed the `finally` block, so `host.stop()` didn't run on error. Use
  `process.exitCode = 1` instead — set the exit code as data, let `finally`
  run, let the event loop drain. [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] exit code
  is a value, not a control-flow jump.

* fix(demos): relative wire paths + staging in plugin buildStart hook

Two round-3 review findings on vite.config.demos.ts, both about staging:

- Absolute filesystem paths in the generated mount.ts wouldn't resolve as
  module specifiers on Windows (`C:/...` is rejected by most ESM resolvers).
  Use `path.relative()` so the import is platform-uniform.

- Staging ran at module-evaluation time, so `vite preview` (and any tooling
  that just reads the config) re-staged on every load. Move staging into a
  `buildStart` plugin hook — fires only on build, not on preview or config
  reads. [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] the discriminator "are we building
  right now?" is data Vite exposes via the plugin lifecycle, not a branch
  the config has to make.

* fix(demos): expand mount template's Terminal shape to match XtermTerminal

The mount.ts.tmpl declared `Terminal` with only `.open()` and `.focus()`,
which forced an `as unknown as Parameters<typeof mount>[0]` cast at the
boundary — laundering the type rather than expressing it.

[LAW:types-are-the-program] Declare the full surface every wire's
`mount(terminal: XtermTerminal)` expects: `cols`/`rows`, `write`, `onData`,
`onResize`, plus the DOM helpers (`open`, `focus`). TypeScript matches
structurally; the cast disappears. The type now describes the real shape
of the value flowing across the boundary instead of papering over a gap.

* fix(demos): honest hostStream return type, requireEl, build-only plugin, lint scripts

Four round-5 review findings:

1. **hostStream return type honest**: was declared as the full
   `NodeJS.WritableStream` but only `.write` / `.end` / `.writable` are
   implemented. Narrowed to a new `RichWritable` interface that says exactly
   what's there; callers crossing the boundary to Console's wider `file:`
   option cast inline with a comment pointing at followup
   `rich-demo-site-pek.3.4` (which will widen Console's type). [LAW:types-are-the-program]
   the type now matches the value's real surface.

2. **requireEl helper in mount.ts.tmpl**: replace `getElementById(...) as
   HTMLElement` casts with a tiny helper that throws a precise error
   ("missing #status" / "missing #term") if the shell HTML is missing the
   element. Trust-boundary null check, not a defensive shim.

3. **Build-only staging plugin**: added `apply: "build"` so the plugin
   itself is scoped to `vite build`. The comment previously claimed dev/
   preview didn't trigger staging; now that's a *property of the plugin
   object*, not a property of which hooks fire.

4. **Type-check vite.config.demos.ts**: new `tsconfig.scripts.json` covers
   the build config; `npm run lint` chains both check passes.

Plus one new hostStream test pinning `.end()`'s chain-returns-self contract.

* style(themes-and-color-studio): indent runDemo body to match its scope

The surgical wrap from rich-demo-site-pek.3 left ~820 lines of demo body
at column 0 inside `runDemo()`. Visually the body read as module-level
even though it lives inside the function — a real readability hazard
for anyone editing the demo later. Mechanical 2-space indent on lines
136-956, no behavior change.

* fix(demos): fail loud when wire.ts has no compiled wire.js

Previously discoverDemos() silently filtered out demos missing their
tsc-compiled artifact, so running `vite build --config vite.config.demos.ts`
directly (without `npm run demos:build`, which chains tsc first) would
appear to succeed while quietly dropping the new demo from the output.

Now the discovery raises a precise error listing every wire.ts that lacks
a compiled wire.js, with the remediation command spelled out. [LAW:verifiable-goals,
LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] — no silent exclusion path.

* fix(demos): alt-screen restore on startup throws; build-only wire validation

Three interactive demos (dropdown-demo, rich-config, rich-template-bindings)
entered the alt-screen with `host.write("\x1b[?1049h…")` and only restored it
in `handle.stop()` / `shutdown()`. The bootstrap's catch only calls
`host.stop()`, which doesn't touch alt-screen state — so a throw from
`screen.mount`, `screen.start`, `router.start`, or an `autorun` left the
terminal in the alternate buffer. Wrap startup in try/catch routing through
the demo's own stop/shutdown so alt-screen state has exactly one restore
site that runs regardless of which startup step failed. [LAW:single-enforcer]

dropdown-demo additionally initialises `mutationTimer` to `null` *before*
`handle` so `handle.stop()` is structurally safe during partial startup.
[LAW:types-are-the-program]

`vite.config.demos.ts`: separate enumeration from validation. `discoverDemos()`
now only reads directory names with `wire.ts` (safe to run at config-evaluation
time, including from `vite preview`). The "compiled wire.js exists" build
constraint moves into `stageDemos()`, which is reached only via the
`stagingPlugin` (already scoped `apply: "build"`). `vite preview` no longer
requires `dist-demo/` to exist; `vite build` still fails loudly on missing
compiled wires. [LAW:dataflow-not-control-flow] the build-vs-preview
discriminator is data the plugin lifecycle carries; the config no longer
makes that decision implicitly.

* fix(demos): close LAW marker bracket in mount template

The `[LAW:no-defensive-null-guards exception: …]` comment was missing its
closing bracket, so the observability marker did not parse as a tagged
exception. The CLAUDE.md format is `[LAW:<token>] exception: reason` —
downstream agents grep for that exact shape when reasoning about
architectural ground truth, so the bracket is a syntactic contract, not a
typo. [LAW:one-source-of-truth] the marker now matches the canonical
format used everywhere else in the repo.

fix(coverage): label every allowlist entry by its actual export kind

Copilot review on PR #35 flagged that the reason string for KeyEvent
called it a "type" when src/widgets/types.ts declares it as a class.
A reader debugging a coverage failure consumes that reason string
verbatim — a wrong label is misleading guidance, not just imprecision.

The same pattern was repeated across many entries (I had labeled most
interfaces as "type" and several classes as "type"). Rather than
fix only the entry Copilot named, a derivation pass over src/ rewrote
every reason string from the actual export declaration:

  - class      → "<scope>: <Name> class"
  - interface  → "<scope>: <Name> interface"
  - type       → "<scope>: <Name> type alias"
  - const      → "<scope>: <Name> constant"
  - function   → "<scope>: <Name> function"
  - enum       → "<scope>: <Name> enum"

83 lines of labels updated. Existing parenthetical context (e.g.
"used transitively via Pretty") is preserved.

[LAW:one-source-of-truth] The src/ declaration is the canonical
description of an export's kind. A reason string that disagrees with
it is a divergent copy — fix the divergence by deriving from the
source, not by patching the copy point-by-point.

Verification: npm run lint clean; coverage verifier still green
(4/4).

chore(demos): retire flagship-per-domain spec and typing

Removes the artifacts that encoded the over-fit "exactly five flagships
with strict source-module ownership" model the previous demo-tune-up
design produced. The lit epic (rich-demos-l2x) has already been
rewritten back to the user's original ask (dedupe / expand / consolidate
/ reorganize / tweak — fewer + more interesting demos, with existing
working demos preserved until something better replaces them).

# Changes

- **Deleted `spec/demos.md`** — the 392-line spec that defined five
  flagships with rigid source-module ownership and mandated deleting the
  interactive TUIs (rich-explore, claude-sessions) to satisfy the count.
  Retired in favor of judgment-driven concrete improvements.

- **`test/coverage/coverage-allowlist.ts`** — dropped the `Flagship`
  string-literal union, the `burndown(flagship)` helper, and the
  discriminated-union `AllowlistEntry` (`{ kind: "burndown" }`
  vs `{ kind: "permanent" }`). Collapsed to one flat shape:
  `AllowlistEntry { reason: string }`. Per-flagship comment headers
  replaced with factual "-- from src/X --" sectioning. [LAW:absorbed-variance]
  — the discriminated union only had one realized case (burndown);
  collapse to one shape.

- **`test/coverage/coverage.test.ts`** — softened the file header
  comment (no longer claims to be "the keystone" of an epic; explicitly
  notes the verifier is a *floor*, not a quality measure). Updated the
  error messages and the redundant-entry detail to match the new
  AllowlistEntry shape.

- **`examples/themes-and-color-studio/index.ts`** — header comment no
  longer calls the demo "the flagship"; describes what it actually is
  (a printed-tour reference kept for the color subsystem, not a template
  for future demos). One-liner inside main() and one in-line infra
  comment updated to match.

# Verification

- npm run lint: clean
- npx vitest run: 8838 passed | 7 skipped (328 files)
- npm run themes-and-color-studio: runs to completion

# What is NOT changed

No demos under `examples/` are deleted. All existing demos
(`rich-explore`, `claude-sessions`, `rich-themes`, `rich-themes-transposed`,
`rich-theme-designer`, `rich-colors`, `rich-config`, `dropdown-demo`,
`rich-dash`, `rich-markup-plugins`, `rich-strip`, `rich-template-bindings`,
`themes-and-color-studio`, `shared`) remain on disk; their npm scripts
remain wired. Per parent epic non-goal: working demos are not deleted
before something concrete has replaced them and been judged a
replacement.
